points.title: Backup
points.must: A copy of data on a separate medium, preferably elsewhere, so the original can be restored; protects against hardware failure, human error, malware, theft and disasters.

points.title: Full, incremental and differential backups
points.must: What each copies (all data / changes since the last backup / changes since the last full) and how they compare in time and space.

points.title: Restoring from backups
points.must: Incremental: the full backup plus every incremental in order; differential: the full backup plus the latest differential; restores are tested.

points.title: RPO and RTO
points.must: RPO: most recent data that may be lost (measured in time); RTO: the longest time the system may be down while restored; with examples.

points.title: Rules for backups
points.must: Regular and automatic; the 3-2-1 rule with an offline copy against ransomware; encrypted and physically secure; labelled; restores tested.

points.title: Versions, snapshots and rotation
points.must: Versions / read-only snapshots let a file be brought back from an earlier day; grandfather–father–son rotation.

points.title: Backup media
points.must: At least three of: external disk, SSD / flash, magnetic tape, NAS, cloud — with capacity, speed or cost.

points.title: Cloud backup
points.must: Advantages (automatically off-site, no hardware, restore anywhere, versions) and disadvantages (needs Internet, monthly cost, privacy / law, slow large restores).

points.title: Disk mirroring (RAID 1)
points.must: Data written to two disks at the same time; if one fails the system keeps working from the other; RAID = several disks seen as one drive.

points.title: Mirroring is not a backup
points.must: Deletions, corruption and ransomware are copied to both disks at once, so backups are still needed; mirroring protects against disk failure only.

points.title: Disaster recovery plan
points.must: A written plan for restoring systems and data and continuing work after a serious incident (fire, flood, ransomware, failed server).

points.title: Contents of the plan
points.must: At least three: critical systems in order, who is responsible, where backups are and how to restore, acceptable downtime / data loss, alternative arrangements, testing the plan.
